TI Exploring supports and constraints to school counselors' practices
   through Q-methodology research
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL FOR EDUCATIONAL AND VOCATIONAL GUIDANCE
LA English
DT Article
DE Career counseling; Systems theory; Q methodology
ID CAREER
AB This Q study explored the systems of influence on 24 male career counselors' practices in Qatari public schools along intrapersonal, relational, and contextual dimensions. Results revealed three perspectives, which differed on the basis of the loci of supports. Accordingly, relationships matter most for F-1, professional goals and values matter most for F-2, and work conditions matter most for F-3. There was also a high level of consensus among factors, revealing shared viewpoints on the supports and constraints to participants' practices. These results are discussed in light of the status of career counseling and the importance of research emerging from the Global South.

TI From secondary school to college: evolution of vocational indecision and
   contributions of motivations in vocational decision-making
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL FOR EDUCATIONAL AND VOCATIONAL GUIDANCE
LA English
DT Article
DE Vocational indecision; Vocational motivations; Self-determination theory
ID CAREER INDECISION; PROFILES; AUTONOMY
AB This study had two main goals: to describe the evolution of vocational indecision in adolescents from mid-secondary school to the second year of college, and to examine how motivations toward vocational decision-making were related to this evolution. A sample of 213 adolescents was followed over a 5-year period. The results showed that adolescents began secondary 3 with a moderate level of vocational indecision, and that this indecision decreased slightly over time. Furthermore, this trajectory was better predicted by controlled motivations than by autonomous motivations, after controlling for gender, having consulted a guidance counselor, and geographical region.

TI Reciprocal relations between self-esteem, class engagement, and career
   calling: evidence from a two-wave longitudinal study
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL FOR EDUCATIONAL AND VOCATIONAL GUIDANCE
LA English
DT Article
DE Self-esteem; Class engagement; Career calling
ID SCHOOL ENGAGEMENT; WORK ENGAGEMENT; ADAPTABILITY; UNIVERSITY;
   CONSTRUCTION; ADAPTATION; IDENTITY; SUCCESS; TURKISH; SCALE
AB This study aims to longitudinally investigate the relationships between self-esteem, class engagement, and career calling. A total of 161 university students were included in the final sample. Data were obtained using the Two-Dimensional Self-Esteem Scale, General Class Engagement Scale, and Career Calling Scale. The cross-lagged panel model revealed the paths (for indirect effects models and autoregressive) between self-esteem, class engagement, and career calling. The cross-lagged panel model demonstrated an acceptable fit with the data. The cross-lagged effect of self-esteem at time 1 on class engagement at time 2 was positive and significant. Furthermore, the cross-lagged effect of class engagement at time 1 on career calling at time 2 was positive and significant. Finally, all these results would support the longitudinal mediation effect of class engagement in the relationship between self-esteem and career calling.

TI Les déterminants de la qualité de l'éducation de base : évidence sur dix
   pays de l'Afrique subsaharienne
SO INTERNATIONAL REVIEW OF EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE qualit & eacute; de l'& eacute;ducation; multiniveau; score moyen; tests
   de comp & eacute;tence; Afrique subsaharienne; I21; I250; C33
ID SCHOOL; PERFORMANCE; EDUCATION; PROGRAM; GIRLS
AB Determinants of quality in basic education: Evidence from ten sub-Saharan African countries - In Africa, less than 20% of pupils achieve scores above the minimum competency threshold. This article attempts to identify the factors that explain the quality of education. The average score of pupils on proficiency tests was used as a measure of the quality of primary education, based on survey data from the Programme for the Analysis of Educational Systems of the Conference of Ministers of Education of French-speaking States and Governments (PASEC). Estimation of a multilevel model using the restricted maximum likelihood method reveals the importance of contextual factors, classroom organisation, school textbooks, teacher training and country stability in explaining differences in pupil proficiency. The results also show that 39.38% of the differences in performance between pupils are due to differences between schools. These differences in performance are also explained by individual student characteristics and differences between countries, at 33.33% and 27.0% respectively. The school environment thus has the greatest influence on differences in performance between pupils.
